B7b-11-double-fertilisation-angiosperms

Diagram of a carpel in longitudinal section showing double fertilisation. Show pollen grains on the stigma, one of which has grown a long pollen tube down through the style into the ovary and through the micropyle of an ovule. Inside the tube near its tip: a tube nucleus and two male nuclei. Inside the ovule's embryo sac: the egg cell with two synergids at the micropyle end, two polar nuclei in the centre and three antipodal cells at the far end. Use two dotted arrows: one from a male nucleus to the egg cell and one from the other male nucleus to the polar nuclei. Soft green carpel, yellow pollen, purple nuclei.
B7b-07-floral-hibiscus

Floral diagram (ground plan from above) of a Hibiscus flower. Show a small circle at the top for the mother axis, an outer ring of five small bract shapes for the epicalyx, then five joined crescent-shaped sepals, then five free petal shapes overlapping, then a ring of many small two-lobed anther shapes joined by a circle (staminal tube), and in the centre the ovary in cross-section with five chambers, each with ovules on the central axis. Soft green, pink and yellow palette.
B7b-01-flower-longitudinal-section

Half-flower (longitudinal section) of a typical bisexual dicot flower, drawn large in the centre. Show from the bottom up: a short flower stalk, the swollen receptacle, two green sepals curving outwards, two large soft-pink petals with a small nectary at the base of each petal, four stamens (each a thin filament topped by a yellow two-lobed anther), and in the centre the pistil: a green swollen ovary at the base (cut open to show three ovules attached to its wall), a slender style rising from it, and a sticky three-lobed stigma at the top. Use soft green for sepals and ovary, soft pink for petals, yellow for anthers.
B7b-02-stamen-pollen-grain-structure

Two diagrams side by side. Left: a single stamen showing a long thin filament topped by an anther with two lobes, one lobe cut across to show four pollen sacs, one sac split open with pollen grains spilling out. Right: an enlarged pollen grain shown in section with a thick spiky outer wall and thin inner wall, a tube nucleus and a generative nucleus. Use pale green for the filament, yellow-orange for the anther and pollen.
B7b-03-plant-ovule-longitudinal-section

Longitudinal section of a mature ovule inside part of an ovary wall. Show the funicle attaching the ovule to the placenta on the ovary wall, two integuments (outer and inner) with a gap at the bottom forming the micropyle, the nucellus, and inside it an oval embryo sac containing three cells at the micropylar end (one egg cell between two synergids), two polar nuclei in the centre, and three antipodal cells at the chalazal end. Soft green ovary wall, cream nucellus, pale lilac embryo sac, darker purple nuclei.
B7b-04-ovary-position-comparison

Three small half-flower diagrams side by side showing the position of the ovary. Left: hypogynous flower with the ovary sitting on top of a flat receptacle and sepals, petals and stamens attached below it. Middle: perigynous flower with a cup-shaped receptacle surrounding a free ovary and the other parts attached to the cup rim. Right: epigynous flower with the ovary sunk inside the receptacle and sepals, petals and stamens attached above it. Labels for each: ovary, receptacle, sepal, petal, stamen; and titles under each: hypogynous (superior ovary), perigynous, epigynous (inferior ovary). Soft green, pink and yellow palette.
B7b-05-hibiscus-flower-anatomy

A Hibiscus flower in side view, partly cut to show its parts. Show the green epicalyx of narrow bracts below a green five-lobed joined calyx, five large red overlapping petals, a long red staminal column projecting from the centre with many small yellow anthers along its upper part, and five short style branches with round red hairy stigmas at the very tip. Below, a small inset of the ovary cut across, showing five chambers with ovules attached to the central axis. Soft red petals, green calyx, yellow anthers.
B7b-06-flamboyant-pride-barbados-comparison

Two flowers side by side for comparison. Left: Flamboyant flower in front view with five clawed scarlet petals, one larger whitish standard petal streaked with red, ten long curved red stamens and a single long style. Right: Pride of Barbados flower in side view with five crinkled orange-red petals with yellow edges, very long red stamens and style projecting far beyond the petals. Labels on each: sepal, petal, standard petal (Flamboyant only), stamens, style, stigma, ovary. Titles under each: Flamboyant (Delonix regia), Pride of Barbados (Caesalpinia pulcherrima).
B7b-08-maize-plant-reproduction

A maize plant shown whole on the left, with a male tassel (branched spike of male flowers) at the top and a female cob in a leaf axil lower down with long silky threads (silks) hanging out of its husk. On the right, two enlargements: a male spikelet with three anthers dangling on long thin filaments, and a section of the female cob showing a single grain-forming ovary with its very long silk (style and stigma) leading out. Show tiny pollen grains drifting in the air from the tassel towards the silks. Soft green and pale yellow colours.
B7b-09-insect-vs-wind-pollination

Side-by-side comparison. Left: a bee visiting a large brightly coloured open flower, with yellow pollen grains stuck on its hairy body, the anthers and sticky stigma inside the flower, and coloured nectar guide lines on the petals. Right: a grass flower (spikelet) with small dull green bracts, anthers dangling on long filaments outside the flower, and two large feathery stigmas outside, with pollen blowing away in wavy wind lines. Labels on left: bright petal, nectar guide, anther inside flower, sticky stigma, pollen on insect body. Labels on right: small dull bracts, anther hanging out, long filament, feathery stigma, light pollen carried by wind. Titles: insect-pollinated flower, wind-pollinated flower.
B7b-14-fruit-classification-comparison

Three fruits side by side. 1. Aggregate fruit: a soursop shown whole (green with soft spines) and cut lengthwise, showing many white fleshy fruitlets each with a black seed, arranged around a central core (receptacle). 2. Multiple fruit: a pineapple shown whole with diamond-shaped "eyes", and cut lengthwise showing the fused fruitlets around the fibrous central axis, with the crown of leaves on top. 3. A simple fruit for contrast: a pawpaw cut across showing one hollow chamber with black seeds on the inner wall. Titles: aggregate fruit (soursop), multiple fruit (pineapple), simple fruit (pawpaw).
B7b-15-cashew-apple-nut-structure

A cashew fruit hanging from a twig, drawn large: a pear-shaped, shiny red-yellow cashew apple, with the grey-green kidney-shaped cashew nut attached at its lower end. Beside it, the cashew nut cut open showing the hard shell (pericarp) and the curved kernel (seed) inside. Soft red, yellow and grey-green colours.
B7b-10-heterostyly-primrose-flowers

Two primrose flowers cut lengthwise side by side, each with a long narrow corolla tube. Left (pin-eyed): long style reaching the mouth of the tube with the stigma visible at the top, and short stamens attached halfway down the tube. Right (thrum-eyed): short style with stigma halfway down the tube, and stamens attached at the mouth of the tube. Draw dotted arrows crossing between the stamens of one and the stigma at the same height in the other to show the direction of pollen transfer. Soft yellow petals, green ovary.
B7b-13-fleshy-fruit-sections-comparison

Four fleshy fruits cut open, arranged in a row. 1. Tomato cut across, showing skin, fleshy wall, chambers filled with jelly and seeds on a central axis. 2. Orange cut across, showing leathery skin with oil glands, white spongy layer, segments with juice sacs and seeds near the centre. 3. Mango cut lengthwise, showing thin skin, thick yellow fleshy mesocarp, hard fibrous stone (endocarp) and the seed inside. 4. Coconut cut lengthwise, showing smooth outer skin, thick fibrous husk, hard shell, white endosperm (meat) and the hollow filled with coconut water. Titles: tomato (berry), orange (hesperidium), mango (drupe), coconut (fibrous drupe). Soft natural colours.
B7b-16-fruit-seed-dispersal-mechanisms

A panel of six small fruit and seed drawings grouped by dispersal method, each in its own rounded box. 1. Wind: a Tridax fruit with a feathery pappus, and a four-winged Combretum fruit. 2. Wind: a cotton seed with long white fibres. 3. Water: a coconut floating on water, cut-away showing the fibrous husk with air spaces. 4. Animal (eaten): a ripe guava cut open with many small seeds, and a small bird eating it. 5. Animal (attached): a Bidens fruit with two barbed spines caught in animal fur. 6. Explosive: a dry cowpea pod splitting and twisting, with seeds flying out.
